agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

import subprocess, json
def run(args, stdin=None):
    p = subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return p
def test(schema, instance, extra_args=[]):
    open("/tmp/tschema.json","w").write(json.dumps(schema))
    open("/tmp/tinstance.json","w").write(json.dumps(instance))
    p = run(["/tmp/tschema.json","-i","/tmp/tinstance.json"]+extra_args)
    print(f"S={json.dumps(schema)} I={json.dumps(instance)} => EXIT={p.returncode} OUT={repr(p.stdout)}")

# more combinators
test({"oneOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "integer"}]}, 1.5)
test({"anyOf": [{"type": "string", "minLength": 5}]}, "hi")
# if/then/else
test({"if": {"type": "string"}, "then": {"minLength": 5}, "else": {"minimum": 10}}, "hi")
test({"if": {"type": "string"}, "then": {"minLength": 5}, "else": {"minimum": 10}}, 5)
test({"if": {"type": "string"}, "then": {"minLength": 5}, "else": {"minimum": 10}}, "hello!")
test({"if": {"type": "string"}, "then": {"minLength": 5}, "else": {"minimum": 10}}, 15)
# dependencies / dependentRequired / dependentSchemas
test({"dependentRequired": {"foo": ["bar"]}}, {"foo": 1})
test({"dependentRequired": {"foo": ["bar"]}}, {"foo": 1, "bar": 2})
test({"dependencies": {"foo": ["bar"]}}, {"foo": 1})
# propertyNames
test({"propertyNames": {"maxLength": 3}}, {"abcd": 1})
test({"propertyNames": {"maxLength": 3}}, {"ab": 1})
# contains / minContains / maxContains
test({"contains": {"type": "string"}}, [1,2,3])
test({"contains": {"type": "string"}}, [1,"hi",3])
test({"contains": {"type": "string"}, "minContains": 2}, ["a",1])
test({"contains": {"type": "string"}, "maxContains": 1}, ["a","b"])
# prefixItems / items with array
test({"prefixItems": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "integer"}]}, ["hi", "notint"] )
test({"prefixItems": [{"type": "string"}], "items": {"type": "integer"}}, ["hi", 5, "bad"] )
# additionalProperties with schema
test({"properties": {"foo": {}}, "additionalProperties": {"type": "string"}}, {"foo":1, "bar":123})
# patternProperties
test({"patternProperties": {"^x-": {"type": "string"}}}, {"x-foo": 123})
test({"patternProperties": {"^x-": {"type": "string"}}}, {"x-foo": "hi"})
# multipleOf
test({"multipleOf": 3}, 7)
test({"multipleOf": 0.5}, 1.2)
# format with assert
test({"format": "email"}, "not-an-email", ["--assert-format"])
test({"format": "date-time"}, "not-a-date", ["--assert-format"])

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command};
use std::time::Duration;

fn parse_timeout(s: &str) -> Result<f64, String> {
    match s.parse::<f64>() {
        Ok(v) => {
            if !v.is_finite() || v < 0.0 {
                Err("must be a non-negative finite number".to_string())
            } else {
                Ok(v)
            }
        }
        Err(_) => Err(format!("'{}' is not a valid number", s)),
    }
}

fn build_cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("executable")
        .disable_version_flag(true)
        .disable_help_flag(false)
        .arg(
            Arg::new("schema")
                .help("The JSON Schema to validate with (i.e. schema.json)")
                .value_name("SCHEMA")
                .required_unless_present("version")
                .index(1),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("instance")
                .short('i')
                .long("instance")
                .help("A path to a JSON instance (i.e. filename.json) to validate (may be specified multiple times)")
                .value_name("INSTANCES")
                .action(ArgAction::Append)
                .num_args(1),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("draft")
                .short('d')
                .long("draft")
                .help("Enforce a specific JSON Schema draft")
                .value_name("DRAFT")
                .value_parser(["4", "6", "7", "2019", "2020"])
                .num_args(1),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("assert-format")
                .long("assert-format")
                .help("Turn ON format validation")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .overrides_with("no-assert-format"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("no-assert-format")
                .long("no-assert-format")
                .help("Turn OFF format validation")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .overrides_with("assert-format"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("output")
                .long("output")
                .help("Select output style: text (default), flag, list, hierarchical")
                .value_name("OUTPUT")
                .value_parser(["text", "flag", "list", "hierarchical"])
                .default_value("text")
                .num_args(1),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("version")
                .short('v')
                .long("version")
                .help("Show program's version number and exit")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("errors-only")
                .long("errors-only")
                .help("Only show validation errors")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("connect-timeout")
                .long("connect-timeout")
                .help("Timeout for establishing connections (in seconds)")
                .value_name("SECONDS")
                .value_parser(parse_timeout)
                .num_args(1),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("timeout")
                .long("timeout")
                .help("Total timeout for HTTP requests (in seconds)")
                .value_name("SECONDS")
                .value_parser(parse_timeout)
                .num_args(1),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("insecure")
                .short('k')
                .long("insecure")
                .help("Skip TLS certificate verification (dangerous!)")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("cacert")
                .long("cacert")
                .help("Path to a custom CA certificate file (PEM format)")
                .value_name("FILE")
                .num_args(1),
        )
}

fn main() {
    let matches = build_cli().get_matches();
    if matches.get_flag("version") {
        println!("Version: 0.41.0");
        return;
    }
    // Handle timeouts (construct Durations eagerly to replicate panic for huge values)
    let connect_timeout: Option<Duration> = matches.get_one::<f64>("connect-timeout").map(|v| Duration::from_secs_f64(*v));
    let timeout: Option<Duration> = matches.get_one::<f64>("timeout").map(|v| Duration::from_secs_f64(*v));
    let _ = (connect_timeout, timeout);
    println!("ok");
}
RS

fn percent_decode(s: &str) -> String {
    // Decode %XX sequences
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut chars = s.chars().peekable();
    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
        if c == '%' {
            let h1 = chars.next();
            let h2 = chars.next();
            if let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (h1, h2) {
                if let (Some(v1), Some(v2)) = (a.to_digit(16), b.to_digit(16)) {
                    let byte = (v1 * 16 + v2) as u8;
                    out.push(byte as char);
                } else {
                    out.push('%');
                    out.push(a);
                    out.push(b);
                }
            } else {
                out.push('%');
                if let Some(a) = h1 { out.push(a); }
                if let Some(b) = h2 { out.push(b); }
            }
        } else {
            out.push(c);
        }
    }
    out
}

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command};
use std::time::Duration;

fn parse_timeout(s: &str) -> Result<f64, String> {
    match s.parse::<f64>() {
        Ok(v) => {
            if !v.is_finite() || v < 0.0 {
                Err("must be a non-negative finite number".to_string())
            } else {
                Ok(v)
            }
        }
        Err(_) => Err(format!("'{}' is not a valid number", s)),
    }
}

fn build_cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("executable")
        .disable_version_flag(true)
        .disable_help_flag(false)
        .arg(
            Arg::new("schema")
                .help("The JSON Schema to validate with (i.e. schema.json)")
                .value_name("SCHEMA")
                .required_unless_present("version")
                .index(1),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("instance")
                .short('i')
                .long("instance")
                .help("A path to a JSON instance (i.e. filename.json) to validate (may be specified multiple times)")
                .value_name("INSTANCES")
                .action(ArgAction::Append)
                .num_args(1),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("draft")
                .short('d')
                .long("draft")
                .help("Enforce a specific JSON Schema draft")
                .value_name("DRAFT")
                .value_parser(["4", "6", "7", "2019", "2020"])
                .num_args(1),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("assert-format")
                .long("assert-format")
                .help("Turn ON format validation")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .overrides_with("no-assert-format"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("no-assert-format")
                .long("no-assert-format")
                .help("Turn OFF format validation")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .overrides_with("assert-format"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("output")
                .long("output")
                .help("Select output style: text (default), flag, list, hierarchical")
                .value_name("OUTPUT")
                .value_parser(["text", "flag", "list", "hierarchical"])
                .default_value("text")
                .num_args(1),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("version")
                .short('v')
                .long("version")
                .help("Show program's version number and exit")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("errors-only")
                .long("errors-only")
                .help("Only show validation errors")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("connect-timeout")
                .long("connect-timeout")
                .help("Timeout for establishing connections (in seconds)")
                .value_name("SECONDS")
                .value_parser(parse_timeout)
                .num_args(1),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("timeout")
                .long("timeout")
                .help("Total timeout for HTTP requests (in seconds)")
                .value_name("SECONDS")
                .value_parser(parse_timeout)
                .num_args(1),
        )

                .long("insecure")
                .help("Skip TLS certificate verification (dangerous!)")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(

                .long("cacert")
                .help("Path to a custom CA certificate file (PEM format)")
                .value_name("FILE")
                .num_args(1),
        )
}

    let timeout: Option<Duration> = matches.get_one::<f64>("timeout").map(|v| Duration::from_secs_f64(*v));
    let _ = (connect_timeout, timeout);

}
